newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul panel to recommend broader financial reform.
newsitem.headline: Seoul panel to recommend broader financial reform.

text.p: A South Korean presidential panel plans to recommend broader financial reform, including a proposal to foster financial conglomerates, a statement from the commission said on Friday.

The statement from the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform said South Korea should allow more business opportunities for securities houses, merchant banking corporations and investment trust companies to allow them to expand.
On Friday, the commission discussed boosting measures, including allowing securities houses and merchant banking corporations to participate in foreign exchange deals.
The commission also planned to recommend allowing over-the-counter derivative trades by the two types of financial companies, the statement said.
It discussed whether merchant banking corporations and investment trust companies should be allowed to convert into banks or securities houses.

A commission official said the panel has yet to finalise its proposal to the president, which the finance and economic ministry would review. He expected the commission to make its final proposal by the end of March.
